# VideoForge

> Self-hosted video editing, asset-free motion graphics and FFmpeg rendering.
> The browser Studio and agent API use the same timeline. No agent-supplied code is executed.

## Documentation

- [Introduction](./#/docs/introduction): One timeline. A browser studio. An API your agents can actually use.
- [Your first composition](./#/docs/quickstart): Create an animated lower third and export it without uploading a single asset.
- [Motion graphics tutorial](./#/docs/motion-graphics-tutorial): Build an animated intro in the Studio, step by step. No footage needed.
- [Authentication & scopes](./#/docs/authentication): Sign in with email, Google or an API key — and give agents only the access they need.
- [Timeline & layers](./#/docs/timeline): Understand seconds, normalized coordinates and composition order.
- [Motion graphics](./#/docs/motion-graphics): Build asset-free animation with primitives and editable templates.
- [Shape primitives](./#/docs/shapes): Rectangles, ellipses and lines with fill, stroke and transform animation.
- [Keyframes & easing](./#/docs/keyframes): Precise animation that previews in the browser and renders through FFmpeg.
- [Motion presets & sequencing](./#/docs/motion-presets): One-line entrances, emphasis beats and exits, with timing you control.
- [Fit & layout](./#/docs/fit-and-layout): Text that wraps, media that fits and a report for everything that does not.
- [Fonts & text](./#/docs/fonts-and-text): A large font catalog, bold, alignment, line height, letter spacing and uppercase — with a fit engine that knows every family.
- [Animate with code](./#/docs/animate-with-code): Drive any property with a formula of time that previews live and renders exactly.
- [Transitions](./#/docs/transitions): Dissolves, wipes, an iris, barn doors and a diamond between video clips.

- [Using the editor](./#/docs/editor): Cut media, build graphics and refine keyframes visually.
- [Animator](./#/docs/animator): Pose clips, text and shapes like a rig, key them on a timeline and apply the result to your edit.
- [Blocks & scripts](./#/docs/custom-tools): Build anything for your edit with blocks or code, preview it, then apply it to your timeline in one undoable step.
- [Agent workflow](./#/docs/agent-workflow): A reliable observe, edit, verify loop for AI-driven video production.
- [Batch operations](./#/docs/batch-operations): Atomic edits, dry-run validation and revision guards.

- [Rendering & inspection](./#/docs/rendering): See your composition before paying the cost of a full export.

- [Storage & durability](./#/docs/storage-and-durability): Where VideoForge keeps your data, how it is backed up, and how it behaves when a disk is missing.

- [Troubleshooting](./#/docs/troubleshooting): Fixes for the errors people actually hit: uploads, renders, keys and self-hosting.

## Discovery

Use Authorization: Bearer <scoped-key>. BASE is the user's API server, which may
be different from this frontend's origin. Read-capable keys can GET:

- /api/capabilities: limits, property ranges, ops, templates and shape schema
- /api/motion/templates: template catalog
- /api/graphics/schema: JSON Schema for shapes

## Creative loop

1. Discover capabilities; never invent operation names.
2. POST /api/projects with {name,timeline:{clips:[]}}.
3. GET /api/projects/:id; retain updatedAt.
4. POST /api/projects/:id/timeline/ops with {ops:[...],dryRun:true,expectedUpdatedAt}.
5. Submit the same batch without dryRun, retaining expectedUpdatedAt.
6. Use committed createdClipIds to refine layers.
7. Inspect GET /api/projects/:id/state?t=1 and /frame?t=1&width=640.
8. POST /api/renders with {projectId}; poll /api/renders/:jobId.
9. Download /api/renders/:jobId/download only when status is done.

All mutating operations require write scope or higher. Keys/visibility/live-watch
management require admin. Keep owner keys out of agent prompts and client code.

## Motion graphics

add_motion_template args:
{template:"lower-third",title:"Ada Lovelace",subtitle:"Pioneer of computing",
 color:"#f6a447",start:0,duration:4}

Templates: lower-third, title-card, callout, kinetic-type, countdown.
Duration: 0.5..60 seconds. Kinetic type: up to 8 words.
Templates compile to editable clips. Text uses an aspect-ratio-aware fit estimate;
inspect long text in rendered frames.

add_shape_clip args:
{id:"badge",start:0,duration:4,x:0.5,y:0.5,
 shape:{type:"rectangle",width:0.35,height:0.2,fill:"#f6a447",
 stroke:"#ffffff",strokeWidth:2,radius:24}}

Shape types: rectangle, ellipse, line.
Dimensions: fractions of the canvas. strokeWidth/radius: output pixels.
Colors: #rrggbb or transparent. Shape geometry and colors are static.
Transform animation: x, y, scale, rotation, opacity using clip-local keyframes.

stagger_clips args:
{clipIds:["a","b","c"],start:0,delay:0.15}

## Safety and limits

- Up to 100 ops per atomic batch, 200 clips per timeline, 64 keys per property.
- On any failed op, nothing in the batch is persisted (422, failedIndex).
- On a stale guarded ops write, fetch/re-plan (409, REVISION_CONFLICT).
- POST /api/projects/:id/timeline/validate with {timeline} checks without saving.
- Dry-run generated IDs are provisional. Committed createdClipIds are final.
- Media draws first, shapes next, text last. There is no general z-index.
- No arbitrary SVG paths, Lottie, expressions, 3D, nested scenes or motion blur.
- Inspect actual rendered frames: font metrics and sampled easing can vary.
